title: SAML assertion lifecycle, KMS operator runbook, and deployment acceptance
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Purpose: Clarify SAML assertion handling across Redwood Private control plane and define operational runbook for customer KMS/HSM operator actions. Scope: (1) PRD-level acceptance criteria for SSO (SAML 2.0) assertion lifetime, replay protection and attribute mapping required for RBAC; (2) Operator runbook for KMS key import/export, HSM-backed key usage, and emergency key rotation for private deployments; (3) Audit log schema and retention requirements for cryptographic events; (4) Sign-off checklist for security, infra, and customer success prior to GA. Out-of-scope: full implementation details of HSM vendor SDKs (eng to produce adapter), and cross-region key replication (tracked separately). This ticket captures clarifications surfaced during scoping review and lists concrete acceptance gates and signoff steps.
acceptance_criteria: SAML assertions issued by customer IdPs are accepted when Signature and NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter fall within system tolerances: NotBefore <= now + 30s, NotOnOrAfter > now - 1s
Replay protection: token ID (AssertionID) deduplicated for 5 minutes per identity provider per region; documented failure mode and retry guidance included
Attribute mappings required by RBAC: 'email' and 'roles' fields must be present; mapping UI will expose claim->attribute mappings and validation will reject missing mappings with clear error codes
KMS operator runbook drafted and reviewed: includes procedures for importing customer-wrapped keys, rotating a key with zero-downtime fallback, and steps to escalate to HSM vendor support
HSM usage: test harness proving signing/verification via HSM (or HSM emulator) with sample workload; latency measurements included and must not exceed baseline +50ms for common signing ops

Audit logs: cryptographic events (key create/import/rotate/deactivate, KMS access, HSM errors) emitted to audit pipeline with fields: timestamp, actor, operation, key_id, correlation_id, outcome, and obfuscated_key_label; logs retained 365 days by default in Private mode and configurable per-customer
Security review: documented threat model appendix added and security signoff from Security team recorded in comments
Documentation: Console UI guide, operator runbook, and customer onboarding checklist published and linked in PRD
signoff_checklist: Product: PRD and acceptance criteria approved
Security: Threat model reviewed and mitigation items closed or triaged (Security reviewer: Lena Vaughn)
Infrastructure/Eng: Runbook reviewed with runbook owner and one on-call runbook dry-run completed (owner: Marco Li)
DevRel/Docs: Documentation published in drive and linked
Customer Success: Onboarding checklist validated with one pilot customer (customer success rep: Jonas Park)
Legal/Compliance: Retention policy alignment and export controls reviewed
SRE: SLIs/SLOs updated and alerting for KMS/HSM errors configured
decisions: Use assertion ID dedupe window of 5 minutes to balance replay protection and cross-region clock skew tolerance
Default audit retention set to 365 days for Private deployments; customers may request shorter/longer via config in deployment manifest
Adopt vendor-agnostic KMS operator interfaces; HSM-specific adapters will live in eng repository under 'hsm-adapters' and be vendor-maintained
KMS key rotation will use a staged key promotion flow to provide zero-downtime: stage -> mirror signers -> promote -> revoke old key
SAML clock tolerance set to 30s forward and 1s backward to handle common IdP skews while preventing long-lived tokens
